title: Will and Would - One Stem
description: See how {je ferai} and {je ferais} share one stem.
can_do: Tell {je ferai} (I will do) from {je ferais} (I would do).
Find the future stem inside a conditional, as in {il ira} and {il irait}.
line: The future and the conditional share a stem: {je ferai}, {je ferais}.

parts.heading: One stem, two endings
text: The future and the conditional are built on the same stem, and only the ending changes. The stem of {faire} is fer-. The future adds -ai for {je}, and the conditional adds -ais.
parts.note: Said aloud, {je ferai} and {je ferais} sound almost the same. In writing, the final s tells you it is the conditional.

parts.heading: {faire} and {aller} in both tenses
text: Side by side, the future and the conditional of a verb keep one stem. For an -er verb such as {parler}, the stem is the whole infinitive: {je parlerai}. {aller} has a short stem of its own, ir-.

parts.heading: Will or would
text: The future says what will happen. The conditional says what would happen, and it makes a request polite.

lines: Tomorrow I will speak to Paul.
Tomorrow he will go to the café.
Il irait au café, mais il n'a pas d'argent.
He would go to the café, but he has no money.
Je voudrais un café, s'il vous plaît.
I would like a coffee, please.

checks.why: The conditional adds -ais to the stem fer-: {je ferais}. {je ferai} is the future, I will do.
It ends in -ait, the conditional ending for {il}. The future is {il ira}, he will go.

checks.ask: Which one shares its stem with {je ferais}?
checks.why: Both are built on fer-: {je ferai} is the future of the same verb.
